packageRules.description: Immutable-ref housekeeping (pin, pinDigest) automerges: it locks the version already in use and brings in no new upstream code.

Group all non-major updates together. The hive merges this group itself once the required checks pass (it merges trusted-bot pull requests whatever automerge says here); only majors wait for a person.

Third-party GitHub Actions (everything except first-party projectbluefin/**) are offered only once their release is three days old, so a compromised release has time to be spotted and pulled upstream before it lands here. Same decision as finpilot#645 and testsuite.

Give action bumps in the four publishing workflows their own pull request. The hive merges a pure pin bump to these files without a person (its pin-only exception), but only when every file in the pull request is one of them; grouped with other workflows, the bump always waits for a person.
Artwork version bumps — do not automerge, let the update workflow open a review PR
Hold typescript on 6.0.x until @typescript-eslint supports TypeScript 7 (its peer range is >=4.8.4 <6.1.0)

Update the overrides block by raising its version range in package.json. Left to its default, Renovate tries a lock-file-only update with `npm install <package>@<version>`, which npm refuses for an overridden package (EOVERRIDE on postcss-selector-parser, #1724), so no lock file could be written.

A major update always waits for a person. automerge false only stops Renovate; the hive merges trusted-bot pull requests itself, so label the update needs-owner-merge (the hive's auto_merge.human_merge_labels default): the hive never merges a PR with it, and only a person's merge lands it. Never use hold, which merges as soon as someone removes it. Last matching rule wins, so keep this rule last.
